title: The 10 Best Cordless Reciprocating Saws
subtitle: Battery-powered demo saws ranked from live Amazon data — cut, prune, and tear out anywhere.
intro: A reciprocating saw (the tool everyone calls a Sawzall) pushes a long blade back and forth to rip through wood, metal, nail-embedded lumber, PVC, and tree branches. It's the demolition and rough-cut workhorse. Cordless models let you use it up a ladder, in a crawlspace, or out in the yard with no cord. Most of the best sell as a bare tool, so check whether a pick is a bare tool or a ready-to-use kit, and which battery platform it rides. Need maximum sustained power for the least money? See the corded list.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER BDCR20C 20V MAX Reciprocating Saw Kit
products.verdict: The best pick for most people — a complete kit (battery and charger included) with 10,000 reviews at 4.6 stars, ready to cut out of the box for under $80. Tool-free blade change and enough power for pruning and demolition.
pros: Battery and charger included — ready to use
cons: Less power than a pro 18/20V brushless saw

products.name: RYOBI ONE+ 18V Cordless Reciprocating Saw (tool only)
products.verdict: The cheapest name-brand pick — if you're on RYOBI ONE+. A capable 3,400-SPM saw with tool-free blade change for under $50 as a bare tool. Add a ONE+ battery and go.
cons: Tool only — no battery or charger

products.name: DEWALT DCS367B 20V MAX XR Brushless Reciprocating Saw (tool only)
products.verdict: The best cordless recip money can buy — brushless, compact, and brutally capable, with 10,800 reviews at 4.8 stars. A 1-1/8" stroke rips through nail-embedded lumber like a corded saw. Bare tool.
cons: Priciest here, and it's a bare tool

products.name: DEWALT DCS387B 20V MAX Compact Reciprocating Saw (tool only)
products.verdict: The compact DEWALT that fits between studs and into tight spots, with a full 1-1/8" stroke and 4,500 reviews at 4.8 stars. Cheaper than the brushless XR if you don't need the last bit of runtime.
cons: Tool only — no battery or charger

products.name: Milwaukee M18 FUEL SAWZALL Reciprocating Saw (tool only)
products.verdict: The pro's SAWZALL — Milwaukee invented the reciprocating saw, and the M18 FUEL is a brushless demolition monster with a huge 1-1/4" stroke. The pick if you're on the M18 platform.
cons: Tool only — no battery or charger

products.name: WORX 20V 2-in-1 Reciprocating Saw + Jigsaw
products.verdict: Two tools in one — flip it to use as a reciprocating saw or a jigsaw. Clever, light, and well-reviewed (3,900 ratings) on the WORX Power Share platform. Great for a homeowner who wants both.
pros: Reciprocating saw and jigsaw in one
cons: Shorter 3/4" stroke than a dedicated demo saw

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX POWERCONNECT 7/8" Reciprocating Saw (tool only)
products.verdict: The bare-tool version of the popular BLACK+DECKER recip — grab it if you already own 20V POWERCONNECT batteries. 4,000 reviews and tool-free blade change at a low price.
cons: Tool only — no battery or charger

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 Cordless Reciprocating Saw (tool only)
products.verdict: A full 1-1/8" stroke on the CRAFTSMAN V20 platform, with a variable-speed trigger and tool-free blade change. Solid 4.7-star name-brand pick if you're already in V20.
pros: Long 1-1/8" stroke for a mid-price saw
cons: Tool only — no battery or charger

products.name: DEWALT DCS369B 20V MAX ATOMIC Reciprocating Saw (tool only)
products.verdict: DEWALT's compact ATOMIC recip — brushless and short-bodied for one-handed work in tight spaces, with a two-finger variable trigger. A great get-into-corners saw on the 20V platform.
cons: Tool only — no battery or charger

products.name: SEESII Cordless Reciprocating Saw Kit (2 x 4.0Ah)
products.verdict: A loaded budget kit — two 4.0Ah batteries, charger, and blades for around $50. No brand pedigree, but a lot of runtime and everything you need to start cutting out of the box.
pros: Ready to use, no platform needed

avoid.name: No-name Reciprocating Saw for DEWALT 20V Battery
avoid.flag: Lowest-rated no-name that only borrows DEWALT's battery
avoid.verdict: A no-name saw that clamps onto DEWALT batteries to look the part, priced like a real one, and carrying the lowest rating in the category at 3.7 stars. Skip it for a named brand.
reasons: No brand behind it — no warranty, no support, and listings like this vanish and reappear under new names. The DEWALT battery mount is borrowed, not an endorsement.
At 3.7 stars it's the lowest-rated recip saw here; buyers report weak strokes and rough blade clamps.
For a little more, the RYOBI ONE+ or BLACK+DECKER bare tools are real brands with thousands of reviews.
If you want a self-contained cheap saw, the SEESII kit above at least comes with real batteries and a track record.

buyers_guide.a: It pushes a blade back and forth to make fast, rough cuts through almost anything — wood, metal, PVC, drywall, and nail-embedded lumber — plus pruning branches. It's the demolition and remodeling saw; not for fine, straight cuts (that's a circular saw).

A bare tool ships with no battery or charger — great if you own the brand's packs, useless out of the box if you don't. A kit includes a battery, charger, and often blades. Each pick above says which.

Yes. A longer stroke (around 1-1/8 to 1-1/4 inch) uses more of the blade and cuts faster and more aggressively — better for demolition. Shorter strokes (7/8 inch) are gentler and easier one-handed, fine for pruning and light cuts.
Brushless motors run cooler, last longer, and hold power under load — worth it for heavy demolition. For occasional pruning and the odd cut, a brushed saw like the BLACK+DECKER kit is plenty.

Buy on the same platform as tools you already own (DEWALT 20V MAX, Milwaukee M18, RYOBI ONE+, CRAFTSMAN V20). If you own nothing yet, a self-contained kit like the BLACK+DECKER or SEESII avoids the platform lock-in.
